# 2026/2027 Harbourline Summer Internship Program

Source: https://jobs.example.invalid/2026-2027-harbourline-summer-internship-program-in-hamilton
Date posted: 2026-08-31T04:03:36.763Z
Location: Hamilton, Waikato Region, New Zealand

Our 2026 - 2027 intern program is now open for applications. An internship with Harbourline provides you with the ideal start to your engineering career; you will have a meaningful, challenging, and commercially relevant project to work on, with support from both a mentor and project manager. Over the course of your 12-week internship you will be exposed to all the operational facets of a high performing high-tech organisation and be paid well while you’re doing it. It is truly the best kick start to a tech career you could ask for. We have 4 projects to offer this year all running from November 2026 to February 2027 at our R&D centre in Hamilton. To be eligible for anyone of our projects you must: Be enrolled in or recently graduated from a New Zealand tertiary education institution studying towards an undergraduate, honours, postgrad diploma/certificate or con-joint undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Software Development or Engineering Have an understanding of basic networking Have the right to live and work in New Zealand and be able to participate in the programme in Hamilton, New Zealand. How to Apply Simply click the apply now button in the project(s) you are interested in below, the application will ask you for a: CV showing details of projects you may have completed as part of your studies, and any work experience Copy of your academic transcript or equivalent Covering letter indicating: which project of projects you are applying for your key area of interest or specialisation, and a statement on what benefits your preferred project choice will have to your studies and future career path. Applications will close Friday 25 September 2026. Following review, the shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview day 20 October on site at our Hamilton office. The Project This project aims to improve packet capture performance for Harbourline virtual appliances in public and private cloud environments by leveraging the Linux Express Data Path feature. All major Cloud provider and virtualisation drivers have support for XDP (Amazon, Azure, Google, Oracle, VMware, KVM virtio). Usage of this technology can improve performance and lower overhead of capturing real traffic in Cloud and virtualised environments.
